chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When you sit in the first two rak'ahs, recite the Tashahhud, then stand up, say: 'By the power and strength of Allah, I stand and I sit.'"

key_terms.فَتَشَهَّدْتَ: when you have recited the Tashahhud (testimony)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication when standing up from the first two rak'ahs in Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes the specific dhikr 'Bihawlihi wa quwwatihi aqumu wa aq'ud' to be recited when rising from the first two rak'ahs, highlighting the transition between acts of worship as an opportunity for spiritual reflection. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on integrating conscious remembrance of divine power into the physical movements of Salah, ensuring that every action is performed with awareness of Allah’s enabling grace.
